claims.value: oxygen and glucose deprivation (OGD rows) / normoxia and normoglycemia (control rows)

claims.evidence: PRIDE/paper: 'human immortalized brain endothelial cell line hCMEC/D3'. Cellosaurus ID hCMEC/D3, AC CVCL_U985, cross-references PRIDE PXD002292 and PubMed 26718731; BTO:0003339 'HCMEC/D3 cell' verified in OLS.
Cellosaurus: 'Derived from site: In situ; Brain, temporal lobe, blood microvessel; UBERON=UBERON_0001871+UBERON_8410081'. UBERON:0001871 temporal lobe verified in OLS.
Cellosaurus 'Cell type: Endothelial cell; CL=CL_0000115'; PRIDE 'brain endothelial cell line'. CL:0000115 verified.

Weksler 2005 (line origin): 'normal human brain endothelial cells were transduced...'; Cellosaurus lists no disease. The ischemia is modelled in vitro by OGD (treatment), not a property of the donor. PATO:0000461 normal.
Cellosaurus 'SX Female' (STR Amelogenin X).
Cellosaurus 'AG Adult'; Weksler 2005 title 'human adult brain endothelial cell line'. EFO:0001272 adult verified in OLS.
'All cells used in this study were used between pass 20 and pass 35.'
'SILAC RPMI 1640-Flex (Invitrogen)' for both arms during the experiment. NCIT:C178973 verified.
'...supernatant concentrates and kept them at -80ºC until use.'

Methods 'Maxis Impact Q-TOF spectrometer (Bruker)'; both BAF headers contain the string 'maXis impact'. PRIDE structured field says generic 'maXis' MS:1001541; the more specific model MS:1003462 is supported by raw + Methods.
'MS/MS (2-20Hz) of the 20 most intense precursor ions... dynamic exclusion' = DDA top-20.

'digested with trypsin'; search 'trypsin specificity with a maximum of 2 missed cleavages'. Single enzyme: the only digest mentioned is 'The two mixtures (experiment 1 & 2) were digested with trypsin'; no Lys-C or other protease in the protocol.
INFERRED: Methods do not name the activation type; the maXis impact Q-TOF fragments only by collision-induced dissociation in its collision cell.
Q-TOF: MS/MS spectra read out in the TOF; mzTab instrument analyzer 'quadrupole time-of-flight mass spectrometry'.
Methods 'precursor mass tolerance of 10 ppm'; PRIDE XML 'Peptide mass tolerance setting' 10.0 ppm.
Methods 'fragment tolerance of 0.05 Da'; PRIDE XML 'Fragment mass tolerance setting' 0.05 Da.

Methods: 'cysteine carbamidomethylation set as fixed modification'. Search output: MOD:00397 iodoacetamide derivatized residue on 3287/3287 (exp2) and 3001/3001 (exp1) PSM cysteines (behaves as fixed); the PRIDE converter's mzTab header lists it as variable and 'No fixed modifications searched' (converter artefact).
Methods 'methionine oxidation as variable modification'; mzTab variable_mod MOD:00425 monohydroxylated residue on M.
Methods '+6Da for lysine'; mzTab variable_mod MOD:00544 '6x(13)C labeled residue', observed only on K (5047 / 2541 PSM sites). UNIMOD:188 '13C(6) Silac label' verified.
Methods '+10Da for arginine'; mzTab variable_mod MOD:00587 '6x(13)C,4x(15)N labeled L-arginine' on R. UNIMOD:267 verified.

limitations: Full text of PMID 26718731 is not open access; Methods taken from the PRIDE sample/data processing protocol text (authored by the submitters, matches the abstract). Supplementary tables not consulted.
No ontology term for oxygen-glucose deprivation exists in NCIT/EFO (OLS, ZOOMA); characteristics[treatment] and factor value[treatment] are free text.
Dissociation method (CID) is inferred from the instrument type, not stated.
The mapping analysis_expN.baf -> experiment N relies on the file names and on search-result titles 'experiment 1 Nm L_OGD H' / 'experiment 2 Nm H_OGD L'; the PRIDE XML files do not name the raw file.

Donor age (adult, exact age not given), ancestry not available. characteristics[disease]=normal refers to the cell line donor tissue (Weksler 2005 'normal human brain endothelial cells'); the ischemic stroke context is captured by the OGD treatment.
Carbamidomethyl is set Fixed per Methods although PRIDE's converted mzTab header lists all modifications as variable (100% of C carry it).
Heavy lysine is +6 Da (13C6, UNIMOD:188) per Methods and PRIDE PTM MOD:00544, not the more common 13C6 15N2 (+8).
